raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On GPUs without native OCP MX support (e.g. MI250X), MXFP4/MXFP6 MoE layers run through `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`, which dequantizes every local expert to bf16/fp16 on every forward. A decode batch usually routes to a small fraction of the experts, so this PR dequantizes only the routed ones when they are at most a quarter of the local experts. Related, touching the same class but not this path: #43983 (oracle test coverage), #52868 (`a2_scale` forwarding).

Related prior work: #40055 by @ekuznetsov139 (open since April) applies the same idea to this class for single-token decode (batch 1, no EP, no biases), using a fixed-size sort so it also works under CUDA-graph capture. This PR covers multi-token batches up to a quarter of the local experts but falls back to the full path under capture, so the two overlap only at eager batch 1. I'm happy to fold #40055's capturable batch-1 path in here with credit, or to rebase onto it if it lands first, whichever reviewers prefer.

## Claims

- When a batch routes to at most a quarter of the local experts, `apply` gathers the routed experts' packed weights and scales, dequantizes only those, and renumbers `topk_ids` onto the gathered set (`torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True)`).
- The output is unchanged: each token is multiplied by the same dequantized expert weights. The test checks this with `torch.equal`.
- Past a quarter, for an empty batch, under CUDA-graph capture, and with an `expert_map` (EP), LoRA experts or w1/w2 biases, the existing full dequantization runs unchanged.
- One MoE layer of a 256-expert MXFP4 model at TP8 on MI250X: 6.6 ms per call before, 1.5 ms with 8 routed experts (c=1), 2.3 ms with 31 (c=4). This is a microbenchmark; see Validation.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark, MI250X (gfx90a), one MoE layer** of a large 256-expert MXFP4 MoE model at TP8, measured on a GCD that was busy with other work (the routed rows include the gather):

| routed experts | time per call |
|---|---|
| all (main) | 6.6 ms |
| 8 (c=1 decode) | 1.5 ms |
| 31 (c=4) | 2.3 ms |
| 100 (gather forced) | 6.2 ms |
| 225 (gather forced) | 15.5 ms |

The last two rows were measured with the gather forced, to pick the threshold. With 256 experts the threshold is 64, so this PR sends both to the full path. The layer output was bit-identical in every row.

**No end-to-end number.** This change has not been served end to end on this base. Before the change, c=1 decode of that model (TP8 x PP3) ran at about 2.4 tok/s.

**Test**, `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_emulation_routed.py` (ROCm only): a real MXFP4 emulation MoE forward with 32 experts. A spy on `_dequantize_weights` records how many experts each call dequantizes; the test then forces the full path (capture flag patched on) and compares outputs with `torch.equal`. Two cases: 4 tokens routed to 5 experts (routed path), and 5 tokens routed to 9 experts, past the threshold of 8 (full path).

<details>
<summary>commands and output (1x MI250X, gfx90a, main 8e2beaa3b)</summary>

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_emulation_routed.py     # with this change
..                                                                       [100%]
2 passed in 42.75s

# without (non-test files reverted to main)
>       assert dequantized == [num_routed, num_routed]
E       assert [32, 32] == [5, 5]
E         At index 0 diff: 32 != 5
FAILED tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_emulation_routed.py::test_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical[topk_ids0-5]
1 failed, 1 passed in 8.50s
```

Rebased on main `db3b0f0fa`: ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean. The test is skipped on CPU and CUDA hosts.
</details>

**Not tested:** MXFP6 schemes (same code path; only the dequantization function differs); end-to-end throughput.

## Details

**Host sync.** Outside graph capture, this change adds one `torch.unique` per MoE layer per forward, which synchronizes with the host. It runs before the threshold check, so batches that end up on the full path pay it too. Captured decode graphs are not affected: under capture the full path runs, as it does today. So the gain applies to eager mode and to batches that fall outside the captured sizes. Making the routed path capturable would need a fixed-size gather (e.g. `topk_ids.numel()` slots), which I left out to keep this change small.

**Threshold.** A quarter of the local experts is where, on MI250X, the gather and renumbering cost about as much as the dequantization they save (the 100-expert row above is already at parity with the full path). It is a constant in `apply`, not a config knob.

**Why not EP/LoRA/bias.** With an `expert_map` the ids are global and would need remapping before the gather; LoRA and biases index per-expert tensors that the gather does not cover. These cases keep the full path rather than growing this change.
AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The OCP MX emulation MoE dequantizes only the experts a batch routes to."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts import (
+    ocp_mx_emulation_moe as emulation,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="emulation backend targets ROCm"
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "topk_ids, num_routed",
+    [
+        # 5 of 32 experts: only those are dequantized.
+        ([[30, 2], [2, 17], [9, 30], [17, 4]], 5),
+        # 9 of 32, past a quarter: every expert is dequantized.
+        ([[0, 1], [2, 3], [4, 5], [6, 7], [8, 0]], 32),
+    ],
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_routed_dequant_moe_forward_is_bit_identical(monkeypatch, topk_ids, num_routed):
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import FusedMoEConfig
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
+        FusedMoEParallelConfig,
+        RoutingMethodType,
+        mxfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp4 import (
+        Mxfp4MoeBackend,
+        make_mxfp4_moe_kernel,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp4_utils import (
+        mxfp4_quantize,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager
+
+    init_workspace_manager(torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+
+    num_experts, topk = 32, 2
+    hidden_size, intermediate_size = 256, 256
+    dtype, device = torch.bfloat16, "cuda:0"
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    w13, w13_scale = mxfp4_quantize(
+        torch.randn(
+            num_experts, 2 * intermediate_size, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device
+        )
+        / 8
+    )
+    w2, w2_scale = mxfp4_quantize(
+        torch.randn(
+            num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, dtype=dtype, device=device
+        )
+        / 8
+    )
+    w13, w2 = w13.contiguous(), w2.contiguous()
+    w13_scale, w2_scale = w13_scale.contiguous(), w2_scale.contiguous()
+
+    topk_ids = torch.tensor(topk_ids, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    num_tokens = topk_ids.size(0)
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    topk_weights = torch.softmax(
+        torch.randn(num_tokens, topk, device=device), dim=-1
+    ).to(dtype)
+
+    dequantized: list[int] = []
+    dequantize = emulation.OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts._dequantize_weights
+
+    def recording_dequantize(self, w, w_scale, dtype):
+        dequantized.append(w.size(0))
+        return dequantize(self, w, w_scale, dtype)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        emulation.OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts,
+        "_dequantize_weights",
+        recording_dequantize,
+    )
+
+    def run():
+        moe_config = FusedMoEConfig(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            experts_per_token=topk,
+            hidden_dim=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            num_local_experts=num_experts,
+            num_logical_experts=num_experts,
+            moe_parallel_config=FusedMoEParallelConfig.make_no_parallel(),
+            activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
+            in_dtype=dtype,
+            device=device,
+            routing_method=RoutingMethodType.Renormalize,
+        )
+        # A fresh quant config per run: the experts null the weight scales on it.
+        quant_config = mxfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(
+            w1_scale=w13_scale, w2_scale=w2_scale
+        )
+        with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+            kernel = make_mxfp4_moe_kernel(
+                moe_quant_config=quant_config,
+                moe_config=moe_config,
+                mxfp4_backend=Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION,
+                experts_cls=emulation.OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts,
+                routing_tables=None,
+            )
+            return kernel.apply(
+                hidden_states=hidden_states,
+                w1=w13,
+                w2=w2,
+                topk_weights=topk_weights,
+                topk_ids=topk_ids,
+                activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
+                global_num_experts=num_experts,
+                expert_map=None,
+                apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+            )
+
+    routed = run()
+    assert dequantized == [num_routed, num_routed]
+    # The routed path is skipped under graph capture; use that to get the
+    # full-dequant reference.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", lambda: True)
+    dequantized.clear()
+    full = run()
+    assert dequantized == [num_experts, num_experts]
+    assert torch.equal(routed, full)

@@ -197,13 +197,31 @@ def apply(
         assert w1.dtype == torch.uint8
         assert w2.dtype == torch.uint8
 
+        w1_scale, w2_scale = self.w1_scale_val, self.w2_scale_val
+        # Dequantizing every local expert writes the whole layer in bf16/fp16
+        # on each call. When the batch routes to few experts, dequantize only
+        # those and renumber topk_ids onto them.
+        if (
+            expert_map is None
+            and self._lora_context is None
+            and self.quant_config.w1_bias is None
+            and self.quant_config.w2_bias is None
+            and not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+        ):
+            # torch.unique syncs with the host, hence not under graph capture.
+            used, local_ids = torch.unique(topk_ids, return_inverse=True)
+            # Past a quarter of the experts, the gather costs about as much as
+            # the full dequantization saves.
+            if 0 < used.numel() <= w1.size(0) // 4:
+                assert w1_scale is not None and w2_scale is not None
+                w1, w2 = w1[used], w2[used]
+                w1_scale, w2_scale = w1_scale[used], w2_scale[used]
+                topk_ids = local_ids.view_as(topk_ids).to(topk_ids.dtype)
+                global_num_experts = used.numel()
+
         # Dequantize w1 and w2 from packed OCP MX format to bf16/fp16
-        w1_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(
-            w1, self.w1_scale_val, hidden_states.dtype
-        )
-        w2_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(
-            w2, self.w2_scale_val, hidden_states.dtype
-        )
+        w1_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(w1, w1_scale, hidden_states.dtype)
+        w2_dequant = self._dequantize_weights(w2, w2_scale, hidden_states.dtype)
 
         # Activation quantization/dequantization is deferred to
         # `moe_kernel_quantize_input` in TritonExperts.apply.
